newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks end sharply higher in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks end sharply higher in heavy trade.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed more than one percent higher in heavy turnover as local stocks absorbed gains in Chilean-issued ADRs Wednesday when the Santiago bourse was closed, said traders.
The bolsa is seen extending the bull run at Friday's opening with the rally continuing to be led by electricity stocks, they said.
The 40-share index closed up 1.45 percent at 123.69 points. The general index gained 0.83 percent at 5,447.37 points.
Turnover rocketed to 31.7 billion pesos -- the heaviest daily volume this year -- from 15 billion pesos Tuesday.
"Most orders came from brokers dealing their own portfolios in the expectation that the electricity stocks will keep rising abroad," said one dealer.
Power shares have been rising since the start of the week bolstered by hopes that the drought is over and by news ING Barings has raised its recommendation on Endesa to buy from hold, said traders.
Heavy downpours in recent days and forecast of rain in the next three months are likely to keep driving Endesa and its parent company Enersis upwards, they added.
Endesa climbed 2.65 percent to 271-1/2 pesos while Enersis rose 0.93 percent to 271 pesos.

Other gainers included supermarket chain Santa Isabel which rallied on news founder Eduardo Elberg plans to sell his shareholding to a group controlling Argentine supermarket chain Disco, said traders.
"It's going to be positive as Disco has a strong background in Argentina," said one dealer.
In New York, Santa Isabel's ADRs jumped 5.58 percent to 26. In Santiago, its stock rose 1.43 percent to 710 pesos.
Decliners included telecom Telex, down 1.85 percent at 1,060 pesos, pension manager Provida, down 1.33 percent at 7,400 pesos, and supermarket group Unimarc which shed 0.66 percent at 150 pesos.
